From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, camila.reyes@redwood.com, stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 11 May 2026 10:22:00 +02:00
Subject: Re: Marketplace listing next steps

Lena — thanks for the clear list. Looping in Marissa (Partnerships), Camila (Product PM for Marketplace flow), and Stephanie (Legal ops) to coordinate. Quick answers up front:

- Publisher account: Microsoft requires the external company (DataScale) to have a publisher ID for co-sell eligibility unless Redwood will be the publisher of record. There are tradeoffs; we can be the publisher and set CoSell permissions to include DataScale, or DataScale can provision their own Publisher ID (recommended for long-term branding).

- Offer manifest: minimum needed for initial publish are: offerId, publisherId, plan sku, planId, planDisplayName, ARM template or SaaS offer URL, and pricing model. I attached a copy of our current redwood-offer-manifest.json as an example.

- Technical validation artifacts: standard items are the SOC2 summary and the network diagram, but Azure validation also asks for a short runbook showing how customer onboarding and support integrates with Azure AD (SSO) + any private link architecture if used. If you have an architecture diagram showing where your API endpoints run and how secrets are rotated, that helps to speed approval.

Action items I propose:
1) DataScale decides publisher-of-record or request Redwood to publish (reply with preference).
2) If DataScale publishes, ask them to generate a publisherId and share the verification email; I can add our partnerships contact at Microsoft to the validation ticket.
3) DataScale to share the minimal artifacts (SOC2 summary, one-page network diagram, sample offer manifest).

I'll schedule a 30-min call with Microsoft validation if you want — Marissa, can you check availability tomorrow?

Best,
Jonas Weber
Head of GTM Partnerships, Redwood Inference
jonas.weber@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0110
